name: Desulfovibrio vulgaris + Methanococcus maripaludis

paper.title: Metabolic modeling of a mutualistic microbial community
paper.authors: Stolyar S, Van Dien S, Hillesland KL, Pinel N, Lie TJ, Leigh JA, Stahl DA

description: The first stoichiometric model of a microbial mutualism. D. vulgaris oxidises lactate to acetate and hydrogen, which is only thermodynamically favourable while something keeps the hydrogen low; M. maripaludis does that by consuming it to make methane. Neither partner grows on lactate alone without sulfate, and the pair does. The two organisms share one stoichiometric matrix with a joint biomass objective.

models.organism: Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough and Methanococcus maripaludis S2
models.reference: Stolyar S et al. (2007) Mol Syst Biol 3:92. doi:10.1038/msb4100131
models.source: The paper's supplementary material, in CellNetAnalyzer project format, supplied to this project by hand.
models.note: Not retrieved here: the supplement is served from embopress.org, which this environment cannot reach, and the four files arrived from the user instead. They were checked for internal consistency — every metabolite a reaction names is declared and every declared metabolite is used, the layer column agrees with the ZM_ prefix on all 180 reactions, and the macromolecule fractions sum to 1 — but not against the publisher's own copy, which is why the DOI stays unverified.

species.name: D. vulgaris
species.role: Oxidises lactate to acetate, carbon dioxide and hydrogen. A sulfate reducer, which is why withholding sulfate is what forces the partnership. 96 reactions in the joint model, biomass assembled from seven macromolecules.

species.name: M. maripaludis
species.role: Hydrogenotrophic methanogen. Takes the hydrogen and formate its partner releases and makes methane, which keeps the hydrogen low enough for lactate oxidation to stay favourable. 89 reactions, five macromolecules.

conditions.medium: Lactate is the only carbon and energy source, fixed at 10 by the reaction file's own measured-rate column (D86); ammonium is free; sulfate is withheld, which is the syntrophic condition. Fifteen reactions carry a measured rate in that column and it is a constraint, not a note — thirteen of them are held at zero, and one of those is the hydrogen leaving the pair, so every electron D. vulgaris sheds has to reach the methanogen.
conditions.objective: The file's own: growth of D. vulgaris at weight 1, growth of M. maripaludis at 0.1, against ATP maintenance at 1. The weighting is the authors', and it is what sets the ratio between the two organisms.

figure.caption: Sulfate withheld at the left edge, which is the syntrophic condition. Giving D. vulgaris an electron acceptor of its own lets it stop feeding its partner: its growth rises, the methanogen's falls to nothing, and the hydrogen and methane go with it. Computed here from the authors' model; the paper is not quoted for these numbers.

reproduces: The joint model as the supplement states it: 180 reactions and 163 metabolites read from the four CellNetAnalyzer files, every metabolite a reaction names declared in metabolites.txt and every declared metabolite used, with the bounds, the objective coefficients and the fifteen measured rates as written.

The D. vulgaris biomass, which the reaction file leaves empty: seven macromolecules whose mass fractions sum to 1, each with the synthesis cost macromolecule_synthesis.txt gives. The sign convention there — consumed positive, produced negative — is confirmed against the methanogen's own synthesis reactions, which the reaction file writes out the ordinary way.

The split between the two organisms, taken from the file's layer column and cross-checked against the ZM_ prefix on every reaction, which agree everywhere: 96 reactions for D. vulgaris, 89 for M. maripaludis, 2 that belong to the pair's boundary rather than to either.
The mutualism itself, derived rather than asserted: the four metabolites both organisms touch are hydrogen, formate, acetate and ammonium, found by asking which side of the model uses each one.

The paper's central claim, as model behaviour: with sulfate withheld both organisms grow and every electron moves as hydrogen or formate; as sulfate is restored D. vulgaris takes it, and the methanogen's growth, the transfer and the methane all fall away together.
adaptations: CellNetAnalyzer leaves external metabolites unbalanced, which a COBRA model has no notion of, so each of the eight gets one unconstrained exchange reaction. That is the faithful reading of "free to enter or leave" and it is the only reaction the import adds beyond the macromolecule synthesis.

The sulfate condition is set here, not in the files. The supplement marks sulfate external, which leaves it free, and solved that way D. vulgaris simply respires it (4.30) and the methanogen does not grow at all. The syntrophic condition the paper is about is sulfate withheld, so the sweep sets it explicitly and shows the whole range rather than picking one point quietly.
The objective is minimised in CellNetAnalyzer and maximised here, so the coefficients change sign. Their magnitudes are untouched.

The model carries no compartments, no formulas and no charges, so none are invented: everything internal is drawn in the cytosol, the shared and external metabolites outside it, and no mass or charge balance can be checked — unlike every other model in this repository.

Splitting the joint matrix into two drawable members gives each organism its own copy of the shared metabolites plus one exchange reaction each, so the app can draw one medium between the cells. The joint model offered for download keeps the single shared pool the authors wrote.

On the map the app maximises one growth rate shared by both cells, which is not the paper's objective and does not behave like it: raising sulfate there leaves the partnership intact, because the optimum has to keep feeding the methanogen to raise the rate they share. The recorded result and the sweep use the file's own weighted objective, where sulfate does break it. The two are different questions and the card keeps them apart.

expected.note: Computed here from the authors' model with sulfate withheld, not figures quoted from the paper, whose text could not be retrieved in this environment. Both growth rates and the methane are unique at the optimum; the split between hydrogen and formate is not — flux variability at the optimum gives the ranges above, so which carrier moves the electrons is the model's choice to make and not a prediction.

name: Four auxotrophic E. coli strains (SteadyCom)

paper.title: SteadyCom: Predicting microbial abundances while ensuring community stability
paper.authors: Chan SHJ, Simons MN, Maranas CD

description: Four E. coli, each missing two amino acids it cannot make and one it can make but cannot export. Only two auxotrophy pairs exist and each is used twice, so what distinguishes a strain is the amino acid it cannot release. No member grows alone. SteadyCom finds the fastest growth rate the four can share and the relative abundances that sustain it.

species.name: Ec1
species.role: Auxotroph for Lys and Met (DAPDC, HSST blocked); cannot export Phe (PHEt2rpp blocked), so it supplies Arg.

species.name: Ec2
species.role: Auxotroph for Arg and Phe (ARGSL, PPNDH blocked); cannot export Met (METt3pp blocked), so it supplies Lys.

species.name: Ec3
species.role: Auxotroph for Arg and Phe (ARGSL, PPNDH blocked); cannot export Lys (LYSt3pp blocked), so it supplies Met.

species.name: Ec4
species.role: Auxotroph for Lys and Met (DAPDC, HSST blocked); cannot export Arg (ARGt3pp blocked), so it supplies Phe.

models.reference: Feist AM et al. (2007) Mol Syst Biol 3:121. doi:10.1038/msb4100155
models.note: The tutorial reads cobratoolbox/test/models/iAF1260.mat. This is the same reconstruction distributed as SBML; that they agree is evidenced by the growth rate coming out identical to the tutorial's to five decimals.

conditions.medium: iAF1260's own exchange bounds, applied to the community as a whole — glucose 8 and oxygen 18.5 mmol/h per gDW of community, 22 metabolites in all. Nothing here was chosen by Coxeter; the tutorial assigns the model's own bounds (EcCom.lb(EXcom) = lbEx).
conditions.crossFeedingUptake: Each strain may take up only the two amino acids it lacks, at most 1 mmol/h per gDW (exRate = 1).
conditions.secretion: Any member may secrete anything, up to 1000 (EcCom.ub(EXsp) = 1000).
conditions.addedReaction: METt3pp, methionine export by proton antiport, added by the tutorial because iAF1260 has no way to release methionine at all.
conditions.totalBiomass: 1 gDW, so the abundances are relative and sum to one.

reproduces: The maximum community growth rate, 0.73599 /h, to five decimal places.
The cross-feeding structure: each strain secretes the one amino acid it was left able to export, and the reaction it cannot export through carries exactly zero.

The constraints, transcribed reaction by reaction from the authors' tutorial: the eight blocked biosynthetic reactions, the four blocked exporters, the added METt3pp, exRate = 1, secretion capped at 1000, and the medium taken from iAF1260's own bounds.
The SteadyCom formulation itself: mass balance per member, bound coupling LB*X <= V <= UB*X, a community exchange space, V_biomass = X*mu, and the abundances summing to the total biomass.
adaptations: Bisection on mu rather than the tutorial's default of guessing a bracket and then calling MATLAB's fzero. The tutorial offers bisection as its algorithm 3 and reports the same answer from all three, so this is a choice among the paper's own options, not a departure from it. It costs iterations: 22 LPs where fzero needs about 8.

Bounds of 999999 in iAF1260.xml are read as the infinity they stand for and rewritten to COBRA's default of 1000. SteadyCom turns every bound into a matrix coefficient, and 1e6 beside biomass stoichiometry of 1e-5 is enough to stop GLPK solving. Verified non-binding: a strain grows at the same rate either way, and the only fluxes that reached 999999 were futile cycles carrying no net mass.
Rows are scaled by their largest coefficient before reaching the solver. Exact here, since every bound involved is zero.
GLPK rather than the CPLEX the tutorial uses.

The community exchange space is one row per metabolite summing the members' own exchange fluxes, where the tutorial adds explicit [u] metabolites and per-member transfer reactions. The two formulations are the same constraint; Coxeter's has fewer columns.
Secretion out of the community is unbounded where the tutorial caps it at 1e5. Non-binding at these fluxes.

expected.abundanceNote: Computed by Coxeter. The tutorial reports the growth rate in its text; these abundances are what this formulation gives at that rate and are recorded so a regression shows up, not as a figure quoted from the paper.

name: Nine-species gut community (SteadyCom)

paper.title: SteadyCom: Predicting microbial abundances while ensuring community stability
paper.authors: Chan SHJ, Simons MN, Maranas CD

description: Nine species of the human gut microbiota on the estimated average American diet, after the host has absorbed most of the amino acids, carbohydrates and fatty acids.

species.name: B. thetaiotaomicron
species.role: Degrades dietary fiber and releases the sugars that feed the rest. The subject of the Figure 4 sweep. 1443 reactions, 1071 metabolites.

species.name: F. prausnitzii
species.role: Butyrate producer; also takes up fiber, held at 5 C-mmol/gDW/h in the sweep. 804 reactions, 596 metabolites.

species.name: E. coli
species.role: The largest member of the nine. 2404 reactions, 1624 metabolites.

models.reference: Chan SHJ, Simons MN, Maranas CD (2017) PLoS Comput Biol 13(5): e1005539, supplementary model9
models.source: the paper's own distribution: model9.xlsx, model9_readme.txt, model9_rxns_params.txt, model9_stoich.txt and simFigure4.m
models.note: 11009 reactions, 8160 metabolites, 42420 stoichiometric entries, 558 community metabolites. The workbook is the primary source for structure; the two TXT exports validate it, and the bounds come from model9_rxns_params.txt because the workbook carries no diet.

conditions.medium: The authors' diet: the estimated average American diet after the host absorbs 90 % of the amino acids, 97 % of the carbohydrates and 90 % of the fatty acids. It reaches the community as upper bounds on 88 of the 558 community uptake reactions, and nothing about it was chosen here.
conditions.maintenance: Every species is held to 1 mmol ATP per gDW per hour, growing or not (ATPM lower bound 1, upper bound 1000, identical across all nine).
conditions.secretion: Community export is open to 10000 on all 558 community metabolites; species-to-medium exchange runs within the model's own per-reaction bounds.
conditions.totalBiomass: 1 gDW, so the abundances are relative and sum to one.
conditions.figure4: The Figure 4 experiment sweeps the maximum specific fiber uptake rate of B. thetaiotaomicron from 1 to 30 C-mmol/gDW/h while holding F. prausnitzii at 5, constraining only the uptake side of 12 and 5 fiber exchange reactions respectively.

x.label: Maximum specific fiber uptake of B. thetaiotaomicron (C-mmol/gDW/h)

figure.caption: Maximum specific fiber uptake of B. thetaiotaomicron on the x axis, with F. prausnitzii held at 5. FDS = fiber-derived substrates.

reproduces: The model itself, imported from the authors' workbook and checked against their own two TXT exports: 11009 reactions, 8160 metabolites, 9 species, 558 community metabolites, 1116 community exchange reactions, 1355 species-to-medium exchange reactions, and all 42420 stoichiometric coefficients identical in both directions.
Every bound and objective coefficient, matching model9_rxns_params.txt on all 11009 reactions, the nine biomass reactions and the nine ATP maintenance reactions among them.

The community exchange space as the model builds it, not as Coxeter would: community metabolites with their own mass balance, species-to-medium exchange reactions scaled by abundance, and community uptake and export reactions carrying absolute community rates.
The community grows on the authors' diet, at a rate inside the range the paper's own Figure 4 axis spans.

The Figure 4 experiment: the 1-to-30 sweep, the twelve B. thetaiotaomicron and five F. prausnitzii fiber reactions, the 31 carbon numbers, the uptake-only constraint sum(C_i V_i) <= C_max X, and flux variability over the eleven targets the script asks for, all transcribed from simFigure4.m.
adaptations: The diet comes from model9_rxns_params.txt, not from model9.xlsx. In the workbook all 558 community uptake reactions are bounded [0, 0], so the community has no food and cannot grow; the TXT export of the same model carries the diet on 88 of them and agrees with the workbook on all 10921 other reactions. This is the authors' own export of their own bounds, not a medium built here, and the import reports every bound it changes rather than moving any silently.

Bisection on mu, where simFigure4.m leaves options.algorithm unset and so uses the default: guess a bracket, then MATLAB fzero. Both find the same largest mu; bisection costs more LPs. options.GRguess = 0.05 is a starting point for that default algorithm and has no equivalent here.
GLPK rather than the CPLEX that SteadyComFVACplex requires.

Not reproduced from SteadyComFVACplex: options.feasCrit (the choice of feasibility criterion), options.minNorm (minimum-norm solutions, set to 0 in the script and so inactive), and the parametric optimisation SteadyComPOA performs, which Figure 4 does not use. Coxeter has no equivalent of any of them and does not approximate them.

The published Figure 4 values are not available offline, so the sweep is not checked number against number with the paper. What is checked is that it runs on the authors' model, constraints and sweep, and lands inside the ranges the plotting code itself sets: growth rate within [0, 0.082] /h and aggregate exchange within [-0.2, 7] C-mmol/h.

expected.abundanceNote: The abundances are predicted, not prescribed: SteadyCom computes them, and Figure 4B plots how they shift across the sweep.

name: Zuñiga (2020): S. elongatus + E. coli ΔpheA rescue

paper.title: Synthetic microbial communities of heterotrophs and phototrophs facilitate sustainable growth
paper.authors: Zuñiga C, Li T, Guarnieri MT, Jenkins JP, Li CT, Bingol K, Kim YM, Betenbaugh MJ, Zengler K
paper.doiVerifiedFrom: Nature Communications article and Supplementary Data 9 at https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-17612-8

description: The phototroph supplies phenylalanine to an E. coli K-12 pheA deletion mutant. Coxeter reproduces the stationary ΔpheA predictions in Supplementary Data 9 from the complete public source matrices, and compares WT monoculture, mutant monoculture and mutant coculture on one editable map. The WT reference is a source-model calculation; it is not presented as an experimental measurement.

models.reference: Zuñiga et al. (2020), doi:10.1038/s41467-020-17612-8; source description iJB785
models.note: 899 reactions/793 metabolites. The artifact identifies iJB785 although the article names iJB792. No explicit repository license; downloaded privately.

models.reference: Zuñiga et al. (2020), doi:10.1038/s41467-020-17612-8; source description iJO1366
models.note: 2583 reactions/1805 metabolites/1367 genes. The artifact identifies iJO1366 although the article names iML1515. Kept complete.
3162 reactions/2547 metabolites; original knockout-analysis network. The archive is not a pre-deleted pheA mutant: b2599 is applied explicitly.

species.name: S. elongatus cscB+
species.role: Phototrophic complementary partner; secretes phenylalanine at the original community optimum.

species.name: E. coli K-12 ΔpheA
species.role: Heterotroph: b2599 deletion blocks PPNDH while the CHORM b2600 isozyme remains functional.

conditions.medium: Exactly the bounds stored in SingleM{4} for monocultures and modelCo2{2} in CM-modelsKO.mat for coculture. The community permits low glucose and citrate uptake; no phenylalanine is supplied externally. S. elongatus SUCRtex_A has bounds [0,0.182], E. coli SUCRtex_D and the sucrose boundary are closed.
conditions.objective: Maximize the saved source c vector: E. coli biomass alone in monoculture; the sum of E. coli and S. elongatus biomass in coculture. No equal-growth coupling or abundance rescaling.

reproduces: Supplementary Data 9 ΔpheA monoculture growth 0, coculture E. coli growth 0.077574047954866 h⁻¹ and S. elongatus growth 0.0348484100758386 h⁻¹, within 1e-8.
Published phenylalanine transport PHEtex_D +0.0143717559943752 and PHELtex_A −0.0143717559943752, within 1e-8, with external phenylalanine uptake closed.
Independent MATLAB/COBRA/GLPK, Python/COBRApy/GLPK and SciPy/HiGHS calculations agree within 5e-13; full source matrices, bounds, objectives and gene associations are retained.
adaptations: The third-party MAT models have no explicit redistribution license. Coxeter downloads pinned, SHA-256 verified originals into the user’s private browser cache; the repository contains its own adapter, map and calculated results.

The WT monoculture baseline is newly calculated from the supplied reference model, not a published experimental rate. Monoculture and coculture use their respective original media, whose differences are retained.
The source artifacts identify iJO1366/iJB785 rather than the article’s iML1515/iJB792. They are not silently substituted or renamed.
The public script uses ordinary source-objective FBA while Methods mentions OptCom. The implemented stationary prediction is not a new OptCom, dynamic or spatial engine.
A malformed PFL grRules string is read from the original valid indexed rules expression, with identical gene associations. The only biological perturbation is the documented b2599 deletion.
Supplementary Data 9 and the article text support the rescue; Source Data Fig.4b conflicts with them and is not used as an exact numerical reference.

Coxeter namespaces identifiers bijectively for drawing and preserves the original IDs in provenance. It does not change stoichiometry or normalize abundances. The map is a subset of a complete calculation.

expected.note: Published stationary ΔpheA predictions from Supplementary Data 9. Experimental trajectories and conflicting Source Data Fig.4b values are not claimed to be reproduced.
